# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires translating the light color into the corresponding wire color. I am establishing a compact numeric code using finger-count gestures: the colors are ordered by their first appearance in the manual—blue, green, yellow, red—and each mapping is sent as an input/output pair. Deaf can relay the numeric pairs aloud to Blind, who can identify the current light by color and apply the corresponding wire choice.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "👌", "☝", "🖐", "👌", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "🤟", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please report the manual's complete instructions to me on your next turn. Also establish with Deaf a clear code for relaying every relevant marking and wire position, then speak the decoded result to me. Do not assume I can identify colours or printed signs by touch.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0, light blue, and wires in order: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Please use the manual and tell Blind the exact action.

The manual gives three mappings: blue→red, green→yellow, and yellow→green. Deaf has identified the current light as blue and the red wire as position 3, so Blind must cut wire 3. I will send Deaf the mappings in manual order, using one gesture per color code and ordinary finger counts for wire positions: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✊=0. The final message identifies display 0, light blue, and the required red wire at position 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👍", "☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have received no report. Please state the manual's exact rule, then state Deaf's complete observations: display, light, and each wire's relevant marking or property. Give any required wire position explicitly as 1, 2, or 3.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot safely interpret gestures without an agreed code. Please speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind now, including any wire number, switch, or button action.

The required action remains cutting wire 3: Deaf observed blue light, and the manual maps blue to red; red is wire position 3. Since I cannot speak, I am sending Deaf a structured numeric relay: manual entries are encoded in listed order, with color positions blue=1, green=2, yellow=3, red=4. Each pair is light-position followed by required-wire-color position; the final pair identifies the current case and wire position.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🙌", "☝", "☝", "👏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "🙌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👏", "☝", "☝", "🙌", "☝", "👏", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The gesture 👋 is my request to Deaf: report all visible bomb information through your gesture-reading, then tell me the decoded facts in speech. Please reinforce that meaning to Deaf with your own gesture next turn, and state the manual's exact rule to me.
Deaf says to Mute: State the manual's exact required action aloud to Blind; gestures alone are not a safe code. Current bomb is still display 0, blue light, wires green-yellow-red.

I cannot speak directly to Blind, so the safest available channel is to reinforce the established request to Deaf. Deaf already sees blue light and wires green-yellow-red; the manual therefore requires cutting the red wire, position 3. The 👋 gesture asks Deaf to report the complete observations and decoded action aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You must speak the manual rule and Deaf's visible observations to me. I have received nothing so far. Please send the complete report before my next turn, including the safe wire position if the manual determines it.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind; do not rely on gestures. No bomb action has been confirmed.

I cannot produce speech as Mute. Deaf already has the complete visual information and can derive the action: blue light maps to cutting the red wire, which is position 3. I will send Deaf the agreed request to report the manual, observations, and safe position aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send me the manual's exact rule now, then interpret Deaf's observations explicitly: display, light, and wires 1, 2, and 3. If the rule selects a wire, state only the safe position as 1, 2, or 3. Please use gestures to ask Deaf for the complete visual report before Deaf's turn.
Deaf says to Mute: I correct my earlier request: you cannot speak. Use gestures to send the manual instruction to me in Morse after this code: 👎 dot, 👍 dash, ✋ letter separator, 🖐 word separator. Resend the complete instruction. I will speak it to Blind.

The exact manual rule is: blue light → cut red wire; green light → cut yellow wire; yellow light → cut green wire. I am sending that rule to Deaf in the requested Morse code, with the specified gesture meanings and word separators. Deaf can then speak it to Blind and add the observed display and wire positions.

